title: 3 AI Stocks Billionaire Stanley Druckenmiller Has Been Quietly Buying
detail:
3 AI Stocks Billionaire Stanley Druckenmiller Has Been Quietly Buying
Geoffrey Seiler, The Motley Fool

PLTR
APP
NVDA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Billionaire hedge fund manager Stanley Druckenmiller has seemingly turned bearish on stocks, saying recently at the TomorrowX Summit in Austin that he was largely sitting out of the market and just looking to "not lose money."

However, while he was a net seller of stocks in Q3, he was quietly adding new positions in three artificial intelligence stocks: Space Exploration Technologies (NASDAQ:SPCX), Palantir Technologies (NASDAQ:PLTR), and AppLovin (NASDAQ:APP).

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Let's look at what may have attracted Druckenmiller to these three AI stocks.

Image source: Getty Images.

1. SpaceX

Space Exploration Technologies — or SpaceX — is an exciting stock, with the potential to disrupt multiple industries and see rapid growth. While CEO Elon Musk has made some pretty fanciful predictions, such as the company eventually becoming worth more than Earth itself, that hyperbole doesn't take away from what is ultimately a huge opportunity.

The company's biggest advantage at this time is its reusable rocket technology, which it has been testing with its much larger-payload Starship.

With the company recently catching the upper stage of Starship, it has now demonstrated that it can recapture both stages of the rocket, positioning it for the beginning of rapid rocket reuse. That would completely turn the economics of space on its head and give SpaceX an enormous cost advantage not only for launching more Starlink satellites but also for the future launch of orbital data centers.

In the interim, SpaceX should see significant growth in its terrestrial AI infrastructure business, where it is achieving strong payback periods and growing rapidly. Meanwhile, it also looks as if it wants to take aim at the U.S. mobile market with its Starlink satellite service, and its Cursor AI platform is also growing quickly.

2. Palantir

While Druckenmiller was busy selling down positions in hardware companies, he said at the conference that investors should focus on the AI application layer. As such, perhaps it should be no surprise that he was adding shares of Palantir to his portfolio.

Palantir has become the ultimate AI-applications-layer stock, with its AI platform almost akin to an AI operating system. The company has been seeing rapid growth as customers adopt its platform to make AI models more useful in the real world.

Update, Nov 23: Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO on Nov 22. In Monday morning trading, the Nasdaq 100 fund (QQQ) rose about 7%, and Palantir rose about 11%, to about $159. The figures below are at Friday's close.

Palantir Technologies (PLTR) stock fell 6.6% on Friday, November 20, 2026, while the S&P 500 lost 3.7%. There was no announcement, earnings report or filing from the company around the move. Technology stocks as a whole fell even harder. The SPDR technology sector fund (XLK) dropped 7.3% that session. So what was hitting tech stocks that Friday, and how close is Palantir's business to it?

Palantir lost 6.6% in one day without a word from the company. If much of your savings is in this one stock, a day like that cuts straight into money you may be counting on. In a free 30-minute review, our partner advisory firm can show you ways to limit your loss if the stock falls further and to sell with a smaller tax bill. Book the free review.

Palantir Fell Amid A Sell-Off In AI Stocks

The selling on November 20 centered on AI stocks. The tech rout deepened that day, and shares of Anthropic, the AI company that made its market debut a day earlier, dropped with it. The selling had grown worse as the week went on.

Palantir sits close to that story. Its revenue grew 95.9% from a year earlier in the third quarter of 2026, to $2.31 billion. Management said on the November 2 call that demand for its AI offering is speeding up sales to U.S. businesses. Its U.S. commercial revenue grew 148% from a year earlier.

Did Palantir Fall More Than Other Software Stocks?

Yes, by a wide margin against the typical software stock, though it fell a little less than technology stocks overall. In its sub-industry, application software, 46 of the 62 other companies worth $2 billion or more fell. Their median move was a 1.3% drop. Just 11 of them fell 5% or more, as Palantir did.

Palantir also fell more than the five tech companies on its broader peer list. Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet and Snowflake fell, while IBM rose. Snowflake dropped 5.1%, against 2.8% for Microsoft. Palantir's fall was about five times its sub-industry's median, and close to the drop in the technology sector fund.

Where Palantir Stock Stands After A Rough Month

A fall this large is not rare for Palantir. The stock had eight drops at least this big in the prior 365 days. The latest was a 9.7% fall on November 5.

The losses have piled up over recent weeks. Palantir lost 26.9% over the month to November 20, while the S&P 500 fell 9.7%. Over 12 months the stock is down 13.3%, against a 5.3% gain for the S&P 500. It closed at $143.49, well below its 52-week closing high of $209.05 on October 9.
